newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IPCL expects better second half.
newsitem.headline: India's IPCL expects better second half.

text.p: Indian Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd (IPCL) on Friday said it expected to improve its profitability in the second half of 1996/97 (April-March).
After a board meeting on Friday, IPCL said it recorded a profit after tax of 2.55 billion rupees for the first half, down from 3.05 billon rupees during the year ago period.

"Despite overall lull prevailing in the market, IPCL achieved gross turnover of 16.53 billion rupees for the first six months of 1996/97 and net profit stood at 2.55 billion for the same period," it said in a statement.
Depressed petrochemical prices, reduced import duties and a steep hike in feedstock prices had led to a marginal reduction in the value of sales and profit," IPCL said.

"IPCL is however confident of improving its bottomline in the second half of the current financial year in the wake of stabilisation of international prices, enhanced volumes from recently commissioned plants at Vadodara," it said.
Production volumes rose by four percent in the first half compared to the year-ago figures, the company said.

It said the first phase of IPCL's third petrochemicals complex at Gandhar on the western coast comprising a vinyl chloride, polyvinyl chloride, chlor alkali and power plant, are ready to start anytime.
"The expansion work to increase ethylene and LLDPE/HDPE (polyethylene) plant capacities is scheduled to be completed by the first quarter of 1997/98," it said.
The state-run IPCL is India's leading integrated petrochemicals maker.
